proposed_title: Prosecutor Email Said Trump Flew on Epstein’s Jet at Least Eight Times, 1993–1996
proposed_description_short: Reuters reported that a prosecutor’s email said flight records listed Trump on at least eight Epstein-jet flights from 1993 to 1996.
proposed_description_medium: Reuters reported in December 2025 that a January 2020 email from an unidentified New York prosecutor said flight records listed Donald Trump as a passenger on at least eight Epstein-jet flights between 1993 and 1996. The email said Ghislaine Maxwell was aboard at least four. This corrects the packet’s unsupported count of 11 and attributes the count to the email; the report does not itself allege wrongdoing by Trump.
proposed_description_long: Reuters reported on December 23, 2025, that newly released Epstein-related records included a January 2020 email from an unidentified New York prosecutor discussing flight records. According to Reuters, the email said Donald Trump was listed as a passenger on at least eight flights on Jeffrey Epstein’s private jet between 1993 and 1996, including at least four flights on which Ghislaine Maxwell was also listed. The report also described other passengers named in the email. The supported claim is that the prosecutor’s email summarized flight records with that count and date range; the supplied Reuters report is the source for the record’s interpretation. It does not establish that the original flight logs have been independently recounted in this packet, and the passenger listing does not by itself establish participation in or knowledge of Epstein’s crimes. The earlier title’s figure of 11 flights and the medium’s 1993–1998 range are not supported by the linked Reuters report, which says at least eight flights from 1993 through 1996. Recruitment allegations are unrelated and are removed.

proposed_title: Trump’s Hurricane Maria visit to Puerto Rico included paper-towel distribution
proposed_description_short: Trump’s October 2017 Puerto Rico visit after Hurricane Maria included a paper-towel distribution at a relief center.
proposed_description_medium: Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico in September 2017. Trump visited on October 3 and tossed paper towels to people at a relief center. GAO later found that staffing, logistics and infrastructure problems complicated FEMA’s response. A George Washington University study estimated 2,975 excess deaths through August 2018; this is an excess-mortality estimate, not a count of deaths individually attributed to the storm. The evidence does not connect the paper-towel scene to response delays.
proposed_description_long: Hurricane Maria made landfall in Puerto Rico in September 2017 and caused widespread damage to infrastructure, housing and communications. President Donald Trump visited the island on October 3. During a stop at a relief center, he tossed rolls of paper towels to people gathered there, an action that attracted criticism and became a prominent image of the visit. The federal response faced documented operational problems. The Government Accountability Office later reported that sequential disasters created staffing shortages, logistical challenges impeded the rapid deployment of personnel and supplies, and damage to local systems required FEMA to assume functions normally handled by territorial authorities. Separately, a George Washington University study estimated 2,975 excess deaths associated with Hurricane Maria through August 2018; GAO described that figure as Puerto Rico’s then-current official count. “Excess deaths” compares observed deaths with an expected baseline and should not be conflated with a count of deaths individually certified as directly caused by the storm. These sources support the visit, the distribution scene, response challenges and the later mortality estimate. They do not establish that the paper-towel event caused FEMA delays, nor do they provide support for every claim about the Jones Act or funding transfers in the original description. The title is narrowed to the documented visit; the response and mortality context is stated with attribution.

proposed_title: 238 Venezuelans Were Sent to El Salvador on March 15; HRW Documented CECOT Transfers
proposed_description_short: HRW reported 238 Venezuelans were sent to El Salvador on March 15, 2025; its later investigation documented 130 cases transferred to CECOT.
proposed_description_medium: Human Rights Watch reported that 238 Venezuelans were removed by the United States to El Salvador on March 15, 2025. HRW and Cristosal later documented 130 cases transferred to CECOT, including 125 sent there that day. HRW said neither government published a list or explained the detention basis, while relatives sought information about loved ones. The reported total and the documented cases are different counts; the evidence does not establish that every person in the group was individually tracked as held incommunicado.
proposed_description_long: Human Rights Watch reported that on March 15, 2025, the United States removed 238 Venezuelan migrants to El Salvador, where they were taken to the CECOT prison. HRW said neither the U.S. nor Salvadoran government published a list of the people detained or explained the legal basis for their detention, and relatives struggled to obtain information. In a later investigation with Cristosal, HRW documented 130 individual cases of Venezuelan migrants transferred to CECOT; 125 of those cases involved transfers on March 15. These figures describe different denominators: 238 is the reported group removed to El Salvador, while 130 is the set of cases the organizations documented. The evidence supports concerns about transparency and access to information, but it does not establish that all 238 people were individually documented as held incommunicado. The original February Reuters explainer does not substantiate this later transfer event, so the corrected record uses HRW reporting and keeps the evidentiary limits explicit.

proposed_description_long: On April 11, 2025, Politico reported that former Blackwater chief Erik Prince and a group of defense contractors were pitching the White House on a plan connected to deportations to El Salvador. The proposal described an operation that would gather as many as 100,000 people from U.S. prisons, hold them at a 10,000-person detention camp, and fly them to El Salvador. The group said it would need access to government immigration files to determine people’s status. These are terms attributed to the proposal in the reporting; the article did not establish that the government accepted it, that a contract had been awarded, or that the proposed camp or flights were operating. The packet provides no support for the original title’s $100 million contract claim or the prior long description’s assertions of implementation, completed deportations, specific legal violations, or hundreds of millions in contracts. The entry is narrowed to the reported pitch and its stated scale, with administration interest left unresolved.

proposed_title: Melania Trump and Usha Vance Visit Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River
proposed_description_short: Melania Trump and Usha Vance visited Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River on November 19, 2025, meeting military families, service members, students and educators.

They met service members, military families, students and educators. Their schedule included classroom visits, student presentations about technology and participation in activities with military-connected children. proposed_description_long: First Lady Melania Trump and Second Lady Usha Vance visited Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune and Marine Corps Air Station New River in North Carolina on November 19, 2025, according to the White House and Marine Corps. The White House said the visit included meetings with service members, military families, students and educators at both installations. At Lejeune High School, the two observed student presentations about social media, artificial intelligence and technology; they also visited elementary classrooms and took part in student activities. The Marine Corps account independently identifies the date and the two installations. The original linked New York Post story covers a different event on December 1 at Joint Base Andrews, where the women assembled holiday care packages with Cheryl Hines. That article does not support the November visit, but the official White House and Marine Corps reports do. The sources support an account of the visit and its activities; they do not show that Donald Trump attended or took an action during it. Cheryl Hines and the American Red Cross should not be carried over from the separate Andrews event.

proposed_title: Pompeo Invoked an Emergency for $8.1 Billion in Arms Transfers to Three Countries
proposed_description_short: On May 24, 2019, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo invoked an emergency to expedite 22 arms transfers worth about $8.1 billion to Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan.
proposed_description_medium: Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announced on May 24, 2019, that he had made an emergency determination under Section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act and directed immediate formal notification of 22 pending arms transfers totaling about $8.1 billion to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. He cited deterring Iran and building partner self-defense capacity. The action bypassed the ordinary congressional review period.
proposed_description_long: On May 24, 2019, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announced an emergency determination under Section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act and directed the State Department to complete immediate formal notification of 22 pending arms transfers to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. Pompeo put their combined value at approximately $8.1 billion and said the transfers were intended to deter Iranian aggression and strengthen partner self-defense. A contemporaneous CNN report explained that invoking the emergency allowed the administration to expedite the sales without the ordinary congressional review period. The event was broader than the original title’s two named recipients: Jordan was also included. These sources establish the procedural action, approximate total and stated rationale. They do not provide in the cited press statement a full transfer-by-transfer list of weapons and services, or document the outcome of every congressional response. The revised text states the three recipients and attributes the rationale to the administration without treating it as independently proven or implying every transfer was delivered.
